invented: Assumes write locks last only one or two milliseconds, without transaction measurements.
errors: Recommends synchronous=NORMAL without explaining that a power failure can lose committed transactions.
Says N+1 queries cost almost nothing in-process, overlooking repeated query execution and data-processing costs.
Suggests keeping the SQLite file as a rollback without explaining that it will lack writes made after cutover.
A.note: Clear and practical, but its performance assumptions and fixed migration timeline exceed the available evidence.

errors: Recommends synchronous=NORMAL without explaining that a power failure can lose committed transactions.
Unqualified deletion of content types and permissions can violate foreign-key dependencies; the migration procedure needs a safe deletion order and handling of dependent rows.
Presents Django connection pooling as a solution for many workers without explaining that its pools are per process and do not impose a shared connection limit.
B.note: Stronger measurement-based switch conditions and explicit rollback limits make this more useful, though its migration instructions need correction.
